# Volume 3 — Chapter IX An Unwelcome Lover and a Welcome Friend

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

The initial term at Wexcombe had passed rapidly, and the second went by just as fast—“actually whizzed away,” Cressida remarked. Every aspect of it brought complete enjoyment to Nell—the invigorating competition in class, the formation and strengthening of fresh, beneficial bonds, the cheerful, small-scale social gatherings, the activities of the several clubs to which she belonged, and the broadening of her outlook and pursuits. Her studies were pursued diligently because she was resolved to secure the Thorburn Scholarship in English. Obtaining this award signified that her return to Wexcombe for the following year would not require dipping into Thirza’s modest savings—an outcome Nell was steadfastly set against permitting.
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0000 }

Hugh was likewise pursuing a scholarship with all his might, yet he discovered abundant leisure to drop by Thirty-eight, St. John’s quite often. Nearly every college function saw him serving as Nell’s escort, and she was aware that gossip in Wexcombe joined their names together. This enraged Nell, but she was powerless; throwing off an old friend such as Hugh was impossible, particularly since he had abruptly become prudent and cautious, as was necessary given the perilous closeness of several Wexcombe youths who would eagerly have filled his spot beside the slim, red-haired coed, whose gray eyes possessed the allure of evening stars. Nell never drew the throng of eager sufferers that accompanied Cressida’s triumphant progress during her Freshman year; nevertheless, a lanky, intelligent Freshie, a cheerful, small, plump Sophomore, and a tall, scholarly Junior all enjoyed visiting Thirty-eight, St. John’s to discuss ’ologies and ’isms, along with merrier topics, with Nell inside the cushioned parlor of that residence. Hugh harbored no affection for any of these rivals, and he exercised extreme caution not to grant any of them an upper hand over him through an ill-timed exhibition of his genuine emotions toward Nell. In her eyes, he had transformed back into the boy-companion from Brierley times, and in that role he could maintain his position against any infatuated suitor who had thus far joined the competition against him. Nell candidly admitted to herself that no one made a more pleasant associate than Hugh; she felt very pleased, as she informed herself, that he had clearly abandoned all foolish notions—even if she devoted a good deal of time to privately pondering the reason.
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0001 }

Just a single unpleasant event ruined that winter. Sitting completely straight on the cushion Miss Ada cherished most, Wilfred Mott queried Nell one evening whether she would give her word “to become Mrs. Wilfred Mott some day.” Following Barney Pullen’ proxy attempt, this failed to startle Nell’s romantic feelings as severely as it might have under different circumstances; nevertheless, it undoubtedly served as another agonizing disappointment. She felt furious as well, believing she had refrained from offering Wilfred any reason to think such an outcome might occur. Yet what else could be anticipated from a Mott, as Mrs. Agatha Sowerby was accustomed to inquire with contempt? Everything about Wilfred’s posture, pitch, demeanor, and language absolutely dripped with Sloanishness. “He was conferring a great honor—no doubt whatever about that. Furthermore, when Nell, entirely unappreciative of the honor, declined his proposal, handling it with as much tact and thoughtfulness as possible—since even a Mott possessed emotions that shouldn't be excessively hurt—Sloanishness revealed itself even more clearly. Wilfred definitely failed to accept his rejection in the manner of Nell’s fictional refused suitors. On the contrary, he grew enraged, and made his feelings obvious; he uttered a couple or three distinctly spiteful remarks; Nell’s own anger flared rebelliously, prompting her to strike back with a sharp, brief reply whose edge penetrated through even Wilfred’s defensive Sloanishness to hit a sensitive spot; he snatched his hat and stormed out of the residence displaying a bright red face; Nell hurried to the upper floor, tripping two times over Miss Ada’s cushions as she went, and dropped onto her bed, weeping from embarrassment and anger. Could she really have lowered herself to argue with a Mott? Was it conceivable that anything uttered by Wilfred Mott possessed the capability to infuriate her? Oh, this represented true humiliation—worse by far than competing against Nettie Scobie!
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0002 }

“I wish I would never have to lay eyes on the dreadful beast again,” she wept maliciously against her pillows.
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0003 }

She was unable to prevent encountering him once more, yet the deeply offended Wilfred made sure that such meetings did not occur at a very short distance. From that point on, Miss Ada’s cushions were protected from his raids, and whenever he passed Nell in the street, or within the hallways of Wexcombe, he offered a bow that was cold in the highest degree. For almost a year, the connection between these two former classmates remained so tense! Subsequently, Wilfred shifted his shattered devotion to a small, plump, pink-cheeked, snub-nosed, blue-eyed Sophomore who valued his feelings properly, after which he pardoned Nell and stooped to being polite to her once more; he did so with a condescending demeanor designed to demonstrate to her precisely what she had forfeited.
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0004 }

A single day, Nell rushed with excitement into the room belonging to Honora.
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0005 }

“Peruse this,” she exclaimed, throwing a letter to Honora. “It is from Mabel—and her arrival at Wexcombe takes place next year—and how does her proposal strike you? My opinion is that it is absolutely marvelous, provided we are able to execute it. Is it your belief that we are capable of it, Nonie?”
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0006 }

“When I discover what it is, I will be in a better position to inform you,” stated Honora, putting down a Greek lexicon and picking up the missive from Mabel. Mabel Colby was among their friends at Regent’s Academy and had served as a schoolteacher continually from that time onward.
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0007 }

“However, Nell dear, I intend to abandon it,” she communicated, “and attend college the coming year. Since I completed the third year at Regent’s, I am eligible to join the Sophomore class. I am weary of instructing in an isolated rural school. At some point, I will compose a paper concerning ‘The Trials of a Country Schoolmarm.’ A agonizing piece of realism is what it will be. People generally seem to believe that our existence is effortless and that our sole responsibility is to collect our quarterly earnings. The reality regarding us will be revealed in my paper. Really, should seven days go by without somebody informing me that my labor is light and my wage is high, I would decide I ought to request my ascension garment ‘immediately and to onct.’ ‘Well, your pay comes easily,’ a certain tax-payer will remark to me patronizingly. ‘Your sole task is sitting there and listening to recitations.’ Initially, I was accustomed to debating the point, yet I possess more wisdom today. Facts are unyielding entities, though as an individual cleverly remarked, they are far less unyielding than misconceptions. Consequently, I merely offer a haughty smile nowadays in meaningful quiet. Really, nine grades exist within my schoolhouse, forcing me to instruct on a bit of every subject, ranging from examining the internal anatomy of earthworms to analyzing the solar system. Four years old is my youngest scholar—whose mother dispatches him to class in order to ‘get him out of the way’—while my eldest is twenty—having been ‘suddenly struck’ by the notion that attending school and gaining a learning would prove less difficult than continuing behind the plough. During the frantic attempt to pack every variety of study into a daily six hours, I would not be surprised if the youngsters experience what the young lad did upon being taken to view the biograph. ‘Before I understand what passed previously, I must watch for what approaches next,’ he voiced his grievance. That is precisely how I feel.”
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0008 }

“And the mail I receive, Nell! The mother of Tommy writes to me that Tommy does not make progress in arithmetic as quickly as she desires. He remains merely in simple reduction, whereas Johnny Johnson has reached fractions, and Johnny possesses not even half the intelligence of her Tommy, so she finds it incomprehensible. Furthermore, the father of Susy desires to learn why Susy is unable to compose a letter without incorrectly spelling half of the words, and the aunt of Rufus wishes for me to move his seat, since the wicked Brown boy beside whom he sits is instructing him in speaking naughty words.
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0009 }

“Regarding the monetary aspect—however, I shall not start with that. The gods first transform into country schoolmarms those whom they desire to ruin!
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0010 }

“Having let out that complaint, I now feel relieved. When all is said and done, these previous two years have been enjoyable for me. Even so, Wexcombe is where I am heading.
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0011 }

“And now, Nell, I have a small scheme. You are aware of how much I hate boarding. Having boarded for four years, I am utterly sick of it. I am not in the mood to put up with another three years of it.
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0012 }

“Now, why can’t you and Honora and I pool our resources, lease a small home in Portmaris, and manage our own meals? It would cost less than any alternative. Naturally, a housekeeper would be necessary, and I already have someone suitable. You’ve heard me talk about Aunt Euphemia? She is the most wonderful aunt in existence, regardless of her name. That wasn't her fault! Her name became Jamesina since James, her father, perished in a drowning accident at sea one month prior to her birth. My usual name for her is Aunt Phemie. Well, her single daughter just got married and departed for the foreign mission field. Left by herself in a huge residence, Aunt Euphemia experiences terrible loneliness. She will relocate to Portmaris to manage our home if we desire it, and I am certain you will both adore her. This scheme appeals to me increasingly as I ponder it. We could enjoy such pleasant, autonomous days.
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0013 }

“Now, provided you and Honora are in agreement, wouldn't it make sense for you, being right here, to search the area and attempt to locate an appropriate residence during this spring season? Doing so would prove superior to waiting until autumn. It would be even more advantageous if you were able to secure a place that is furnished, but should that fail, we can manage to gather some pieces of furniture amongst ourselves and long-time family friends who have attics. In any case, make a decision at your earliest convenience and send me a letter, which will allow Aunt Euphemia to determine her arrangements for the coming year.”
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0014 }

“I believe that is a wise plan,” Honora remarked.
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0015 }

“I feel the same way,” Nell concurred with enthusiasm. “Naturally, our lodging here is pleasant, but no matter how you look at it, a place like this cannot replace a home. Therefore, we should start searching for a house right away, prior to the arrival of examinations.”
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0016 }

“I am concerned that finding an truly appropriate home will prove difficult,” cautioned Honora. “Do not hold high hopes, Nell. Pleasant dwellings in pleasant neighborhoods are bound to exceed our budget. It is probable that we must settle for a worn small residence along a road inhabited by folks whose acquaintance brings obscurity, and let our interior living make up for the exterior.”
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0017 }

Consequently, house-hunting became their pursuit, yet discovering precisely what suited them turned out to be more difficult than Honora had anticipated. A abundance of dwellings existed, both with furniture and without; nevertheless, a particular one was excessively large, whereas another was excessively small; a certain one cost too much, while another was located at too great a distance from Wexcombe. Examinations occurred and concluded; the final week of the term arrived and yet their “house o’dreams,” to use Nell’s phrase, continued to be a castle in the air.
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0018 }

“I guess we will be forced to yield and delay until autumn,” Honora stated exhausted, while they strolled about the park during a most lovely April day filled with wind and azure, at a time when the harbor churned white and glinted below the pearly fogs drifting above it. “Perhaps we will locate a hovel to house us at that time; and should we fail, we will forever possess boardinghouses.”
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0019 }

“At any rate, I won’t fret over that at the present moment and ruin such a wonderful afternoon,” Nell declared, looking about herself joyfully. Pine balsam gave a subtle scent to the brisk, cold atmosphere, while an immense upside-down bowl of favor—the sky overhead—was entirely clear and blue. “My blood is filled with the song of spring today, and April’s call can be felt throughout the air. Nonie, I am experiencing visions and indulging in dreams. The westerly origin of the wind accounts for that. The west wind is something I truly adore. Doesn't it chant about joy and hope? Whenever an easterly breeze blows, my thoughts invariably turn to doleful waves washing a slate-colored coastline and mournful rain falling on the roof eaves. Should the wind come from the east once I grow elderly, I am going to suffer from rheumatism.”
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0020 }

“And isn’t it wonderful when you shed furs and heavy winter clothes for the first time and step out, like this, in spring clothes?” asked a laughing Honora. “Don’t you feel as though you have been transformed into someone brand new?”
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0021 }

“Spring makes all things new,” remarked Nell. “Furthermore, springs themselves are constantly so fresh. Not a single spring ever mirrors another spring precisely. Each one possesses a unique quality that creates its own distinctive charm. Look at the grass’s deep green color encircling that small pond, and observe the willow buds opening up.”
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0022 }

“And tests are finished and past—the period of Convocation approaches shortly—on coming Wednesday. Seven days from now we shall be back home.”
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0023 }

“I’m glad,” Nell said dreamily. “So many things exist that I want to do. Sitting on the steps of the back porch and feeling the wind blow down across the fields of Mr. Pettifer is something I want. Hunting ferns within the Whispering Wood and gathering violets inside Primrose Dell are things I want. Honora, do you remember the day when we had our golden picnic? Hearing the singing of the frogs and the whispering of the poplars is what I want. However, I have also learned to love Portmaris, and returning next fall makes me glad. Had I not won the Thorburn, I do not believe I could have. Taking any part of the little hoard belonging to Thirza is something I couldn’t do.”
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0024 }

“If we were just able to discover a home!” Honora uttered with a sigh. “Direct your gaze over to Portmaris, Nell—there are houses all around, yet none available for us.”
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0025 }

“Cease, Nonie. ‘The best is yet to be.’ In the manner of the ancient Roman, we will discover a home or construct one. On an occasion such as this, fail is not a word present in my luminous lexicon.”
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0026 }

Remaining in the park until the sun went down, they existed within the astonishing miracle, glory, and wonder of the spring season; and, taking their customary route back by way of Linden Avenue, they traveled so that they could experience the joy of viewing Tabby’s Place.
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0027 }

“I have a sensation like a strange occurrence is about to take place immediately—‘by the pricking of my thumbs,’” Nell remarked while they climbed the incline. “It is a pleasant, tale-like sensation. Oh—oh—oh! Honora Hollis, glance in that direction and inform me whether it is real, or if I am imagining it?”
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0028 }

Honora directed her gaze to the spot. The thumbs and eyes of Nell had spoken the truth. Above the arched entrance to Tabby’s Place, a modest, small sign hung loosely. The words read, “To Let, Furnished. Inquire Within.”
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0029 }

“Honora,” Nell murmured softly, “is there any chance, do you think, that Tabby’s Place could be rented by us?”
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0030 }

“No, I don’t,” Honora stated. “That would be far too good to be real. Modern life doesn't feature fairy tales. Nell, I refuse to hope. Facing the disappointment would be utterly unbearable. Their asking price is bound to exceed our budget. Keep in mind its location on Linden Avenue.”
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0031 }

“Anyhow, we have to discover it,” Nell stated with determination. “Calling tonight is out of the question because it is too late, but our visit will be tomorrow. Oh, Nonie, if acquiring this lovely location is possible! Ever since my initial sight of Tabby’s Place, I’ve constantly had the feeling that my destiny was connected to it.”
{: #nw-v03-c09-p0032 }
